episodes.description: Why do traffic jams appear when there's no accident? In a 2008 experiment, 22 cars driving in a circle formed a stop-and-go jam all by themselves. Here's how one small tap of the brakes grows into a wave that travels backwards, and how one smooth driver can calm it.
episodes.caption: The traffic jam with no cause, explained in clay.

episodes.title: Why Your Brain Hides a Blind Spot 10 Moons Wide
known_issues: Hook scored WORKABLE (57) on hookscore.py; weakest property is specificity
Scene 3 captions: the STT matched 86% of the line (it hears 'Edmey Marriott'), so a few word timings in that scene are interpolated; the caption text itself is the script's spelling

Striped-wall set came back with a stray red fleck and a red roller; regenerated with no red so the red dot stays the only red

episodes.credits_note: Narration 8 takes, 9 images, 6 minimax_h3 scenes (120), 2 thumbnails; balance 585.9 -> 415.85
episodes.description: Why can't you see your blind spot? Every eye has a patch where the optic nerve leaves, with no light-detecting cells at all, and it's wider than ten full moons. Here's how your brain fills that gap with the colours and patterns around it, and how to find yours: cover your left eye, stare at a cross, and watch a dot vanish.
episodes.caption: The hole in your vision you've never noticed, explained in clay.
episodes.overlays: 14 text and diagram overlays drawn by channel/tools/overlays.py, including a new to-scale blind-spot diagram (`field`)
